function.exposition.description: Introduces or clarifies story-relevant setting, situation, character state, or premise.

function.setup.description: Establishes a commitment, condition, object, goal, problem, or expectation that later narrative material may depend on.

function.progression.description: Advances an already established situation, action line, or goal without necessarily changing its direction.

function.complication.description: Introduces a new obstacle, problem, uncertainty, or burden that makes an established line harder.

function.escalation.description: Raises stakes, intensity, cost, urgency, or scope of an existing conflict or problem.

function.reversal.description: Materially changes the apparent direction, expectation, advantage, or interpretation of an established line.

function.turning_point.description: Produces a durable change in the direction or state of a narrative line, supported by downstream consequences.

function.climax.description: Represents a locally culminating high-consequence confrontation or decision for a narrative component; never inferred from position alone.

function.resolution.description: Resolves or settles an established conflict, goal, uncertainty, or dependency.

function.aftermath.description: Shows consequences, adjustment, recovery, or reflection after a resolved/high-impact development.

function.transition.description: Bridges narrative situations, locations, phases, or activity lines without itself carrying major consequence.

function.foreshadowing.description: Provides information or a commitment whose narrative relevance is primarily realized by a later supported event.

function.payoff.description: Later event that concretely realizes, resolves, or activates an earlier supported setup/foreshadowing dependency.

function.callback.description: Later material that meaningfully reuses or refers back to an earlier event/state without necessarily resolving it.
